title: How does 'people liked A' become a number?
hook: People prefer answer A three times out of four. How big is A's reward lead?

knows: that models can be trained with rewards
that people can compare two answers and pick one
doesNotKnow: how pairwise human preferences become reward numbers

misconception: A reward model stores a score each human gave.
objective: The learner can explain that a reward model is fitted so that the gap between two answers' rewards reproduces how often people preferred one, so 3-to-1 odds mean a gap of ln 3 ≈ 1.1, and that it learns only from who won, not why.

claims.text: If P(A preferred) = 1 / (1 + e^−gap) and people pick A 75% of the time, the gap is ln 3 = 1.10 (odds 3 to 1); a gap of 1 predicts 73.1%, 0.75 predicts 67.9%, and 3 predicts 95.3%.
claims.source: Solve sigmoid(g) = 0.75: e^g = 0.75/0.25 = 3, g = ln 3 = 1.0986. Node output of sigmoid() and fittedGap() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: This rule (the chance one item beats another depends only on the difference of their scores through a logistic curve) is the Bradley-Terry model.
claims.source: Bradley & Terry 1952, 'Rank analysis of incomplete block designs: I. The method of paired comparisons', Biometrika 39(3/4).

claims.text: Reward models used to train language models are fitted to human comparisons of answer pairs with this rule; they see who won each comparison, not the reasons.
claims.source: About real systems: Christiano et al. 2017, 'Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences' (NeurIPS); Ouyang et al. 2022, 'Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback' (InstructGPT, NeurIPS), §3.5 reward-model loss.

claims.text: The single pair of answers and the 75% rate are invented for the toy.
claims.source: Brief 29 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; labelled on the stage.

recall.question: Raters prefer answer X over answer Y about half the time. What reward gap will a fitted reward model give them?
options: About 0: they get nearly the same reward
It depends on the scores the raters wrote down
recall.why: The reward model only reproduces win rates. A 50% win rate means even odds, and the logistic curve gives 50% at a gap of 0. Raters give no scores, only picks.
